test_title: PYST 3: RRB Group D - GA (Held On: 27 Nov, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Indicating a strong push toward sustainable energy development, the installed renewable energy generating capacity in India increased from 64.04 watts per capita in 2014-15 to what level per capita in 2024-25?
solution:
The correct answer is __**156.31 watts**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India's **installed renewable energy generating capacity** has seen a significant increase from **64.04 watts per capita** in **2014-15** to **156.31 watts per capita** in **2024-25**, indicating a strong push toward sustainable energy development.
 
• This growth aligns with India's commitment to achieve **450 GW of renewable energy capacity** by **2030**, as part of its **Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC)** under the Paris Agreement.
 
• The transition has been driven by initiatives like the **National Solar Mission**, **National Wind-Solar Hybrid Policy**, and **Green Energy Corridor Project**, which aim to enhance renewable energy adoption and infrastructure.
 
• India has become one of the largest producers of renewable energy globally, leveraging resources such as **solar power, wind energy, hydropower**, and **biomass energy**.
 
• Among the renewable sources, **solar energy** has seen the most rapid growth, with India emerging as the **fourth largest solar power producer** in the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Solar Mission:**

 
 
• Launched in **2010**, it aims to achieve **100 GW of solar power** capacity by **2022**.
 
• India has developed large-scale solar parks like the **Bhadla Solar Park** in Rajasthan, which is one of the world's largest solar parks.
 
• The mission also promotes decentralized solar applications such as rooftop solar systems and off-grid solar solutions.
 
 
 
• **Green Energy Corridor Project:**
 
 
• This project facilitates the integration of renewable energy into the grid by strengthening transmission infrastructure.
 
• It covers states with high renewable energy potential like **Rajasthan, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, and Karnataka**.
 
• The project is supported by financing from international organizations like the **Asian Development Bank** and **KfW Development Bank**.
 
 
 
• **India's Renewable Energy Commitments:**
 
 
• India committed to achieving **50% of its energy requirements** from renewable sources by **2030** during the **COP26 summit** in Glasgow.
 
• The country aims to reduce its carbon intensity by **33%-35%** by 2030, compared to 2005 levels.
 
 
 
• **Global Renewable Energy Status:**
 
 
• India ranks **fourth globally** in installed renewable energy capacity, following **China, the USA, and Germany**.
 
• Globally, renewable energy accounts for over **30% of electricity generation**, with solar and wind leading the charge.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Paris Agreement:**

 
 
• India's renewable energy targets are aligned with its obligations under the **Paris Agreement**, signed in **2015**.
 
• The agreement aims to limit global warming to **below 2°C**, with efforts to restrict it to **1.5°C**.
 
 
 
• **International Solar Alliance (ISA):**
 
 
• Launched by India and France in **2015**, the ISA promotes solar energy deployment in **121 tropical countries**.
 
• It aims to mobilize **$1 trillion** in investments by **2030** for solar energy projects.
 
 
 
• **Renewable Energy Financing:**
 
 
• India has received funding from international institutions like the **World Bank** and **ADB** for renewable energy projects.
 
• Domestic financing mechanisms like **Renewable Energy Development Fund** and **Viability Gap Funding (VGF)** have supported infrastructure development.
 
 
 
• **Challenges:**
 
 
• Despite progress, challenges include **grid integration**, **storage solutions**, and **high initial costs** of renewable projects.
 
• Policies like **Renewable Purchase Obligations (RPOs)** aim to overcome these issues by mandating power utilities to purchase renewable energy.
